_about: The indicator classifier's cases (R78). One file, two readers:
classifier the API looks up with, and `apps/web/lib/indicators.test.ts`
runs the same cases against the TypeScript one the page marks up with.
Two implementations are unavoidable — the lookup happens in Python and the
spans have to be known at render time in TypeScript — so this file is what
stops them disagreeing about what an indicator is.
`classify` maps a whole string to a kind or null. `scan` maps a longer
string to the spans inside it, as [value, kind] pairs in order.
The refusals matter more than the matches: `j.rivera` is an account in
this estate, and a classifier loose enough to call it a domain would make
every identifier on a public page a question about which accounts exist.

Defanged forms are classified too (R115): the page renders `45[.]61[.]184[.]22`, and an indicator nobody can click because it is written the safe way would be the enrichment switched off by the defanging.
